q: The effect is called ____ and it is the physics behind the generators that provide the electricity used in our modern society.
e: The effect is called electromagnetic induction and it is the physics behind the generators that provide the electricity used in our modern society. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field.

q: The discovery of electromagnetic induction was made in ____ by Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry working independently at the same time.
e: The discovery of electromagnetic induction was made in 1831 by Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry working independently at the same time. One farad is one coulomb per volt, so practical capacitors are µF, nF or pF. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.

q: Electric current can be classified as two types: direct current (DC) and ____.
e: Electric current can be classified as two types: direct current (DC) and alternating current (AC). AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery.

q: The direct current is a steady ____ current.
e: The direct current is a steady unidirectional current. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: In a direct current the electrons flow steadily in the same direction all the ____.
e: In a direct current the electrons flow steadily in the same direction all the time. DC keeps one direction, the steady flow you get from a battery. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

q: An alternating current is a current that reverses its direction at regular time ____.
e: An alternating current is a current that reverses its direction at regular time intervals. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: In the alternating current the direction of the flow of electrons changes ____.
e: In the alternating current the direction of the flow of electrons changes periodically. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

q: In Japan and in the most of America, the voltage is between 100 V and ____ V.
e: In Japan and in the most of America, the voltage is between 100 V and 120 V. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The value 100 V is the figure this statement is using.

q: Europe and most other countries in the world (including Myanmar) use a voltage between 220V and ____ V.
e: Europe and most other countries in the world (including Myanmar) use a voltage between 220V and 240 V. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. The value 220V is the figure this statement is using.

q: The frequency of AC current is 50 Hz/60 Hz in Japan, 60 Hz in US and ____ Hz in Europe and most other parts of the world.
e: The frequency of AC current is 50 Hz/60 Hz in Japan, 60 Hz in US and 50 Hz in Europe and most other parts of the world. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

e: When a coil of wire having quite a few turns is rotated a few cycles per second continuously in a magnetic field, an emf is induced in the coil. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. In a ____ field, an emf is induced in the coil. magnetic.

e: The angular velocity ω is equal to 2 pi f, where f is the frequency of the emf. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. 2 pi f, where f is the ____ of the emf. frequency.

q: Therefore, a rotating coil in a magnetic field is the basic of an ____ generator.
e: Therefore, a rotating coil in a magnetic field is the basic of an AC generator. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field.

q: The magnitude of an alternating current at any instant varies precisely the same way as shown by Eq. (11.1) and is given by $I = $ ____.
e: The magnitude of an alternating current at any instant varies precisely the same way as shown by Eq. (11. 1) and is given by I = Im sin ω t. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

q: The alternating current is universally used for household lighting, heating, cooking and other domestic ____.
e: The alternating current is universally used for household lighting, heating, cooking and other domestic functions. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current.

q: The advantage of alternating current is that it is relatively easy to change the ____ of the current.
e: The advantage of alternating current is that it is relatively easy to change the voltage of the current. AC reverses on a clock; household supply is this reversing current. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: The inevitable loss of energy that occurs when current is distributed over long distances is far smaller with alternating current (at high voltage and low current) than with ____ current.
e: The inevitable loss of energy that occurs when current is distributed over long distances is far smaller with alternating current (at high voltage and low current) than with direct current. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.
